programme.title: Jane Austen: The Unseen Portrait?
programme.desc: Martha Kearney meets biographer Paula Byrne, who believes she has found a painting of the author lost to the world for almost two centuries. Art historians and Austen experts scrutinise the portrait and perform forensic analysis as they look to confirm its validity, and Kearney debates how it could change people's views of the writer and what it might reveal about her life

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Paul Rose recounts the story of how American submarine USS Squalus became stranded in the Atlantic in 1939 after a fault caused a partial flooding of the vessel and the deaths of 26 men. The surviving 33 crew members were rescued by divers under the direction of inventor Charles Momsen, employing his pioneering underwater escape apparatus

programme.title: Horizon
programme.sub-title: The Wildest Weather in the Universe: Horizon
programme.desc: Documentary following scientists conducting research into weather on other planets, using unmanned spacecraft to study the solar system and the latest telescopes to examine distant worlds. Their findings have revealed strange phenomena including rains of precious stones, supersonic winds, storms that encompass entire worlds, and temperatures so hot that the clouds are formed of lava

programme.title: Bill Oddie Goes Wild
programme.sub-title: The Best of Bill Oddie Goes Wild
programme.desc: On his home patch of Hampstead Heath in London, Bill reminisces about his past travels in search of the best of British wildlife. He muses over some of his most memorable moments, and revisit some of his highlights, low points and outtakes from the three series of his wildlife show. First broadcast in 2003

programme.title: Birding with Bill Oddie
programme.desc: Bill revisits his childhood birding haunts to discover how they have changed over 50 years, finding out if the same species still frequent the area. First broadcast in 1998

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Katie Derham presents a celebration of moments that made Proms history, with landmark premieres and remarkable debuts, including the first appearances of artists, orchestras and even instruments. Featuring a Betsy Jolas debut inspired by Shakespeare's Tempest, music from the Spanish National Orchestra,, soprano Angel Blue's triumphant first appearance, and the first accordion soloist to grace the Last Night of the Proms stage with Ksenija Sidorova's rendition of Piazzolla's Libertango

programme.title: Black Watch
programme.desc: A 2007 performance of the National Theatre of Scotland's play, filmed in Dingwall. The story is based on interviews conducted by writer Gregory Burke with former soldiers who served in Iraq, recounting events experienced on the ground and discovering what it means to be part of the war on terror and to be able to come home again. Brian Ferguson stars

programme.title: Black Watch: A Soldier's Story
programme.desc: An insight into the National Theatre of Scotland's play as it toured the country in 2007, and as events at home and abroad increased its topical relevance and intensified its emotional impact. Featuring contributions from the show's creator Gregory Burke, director John Tiffany, actor Peter Mullan, and then-Defence Secretary Geoff Hoon

programme.title: The Flying Gardener

programme.title: The Art of Spain
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon concludes his journey in northern Spain, where modern art by masters such as Pablo Picasso, Joan Miro and Salvador Dali flourished in the 20th century. These visionaries produced work that pushed the boundaries of the discipline, while also reflecting the tumultuous social and political events of the century, culminating in the rise and fall of fascism under General Franco

programme.title: Art on the BBC
programme.sub-title: Michelangelo: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
programme.desc: Michelangelo was not merely a giant of the Renaissance. He was also one of the era's most controversial personalities. Art historian Sona Datta explores six decades of BBC archive to discover how TV has influenced our understanding of him. Sona reveals how TV has tried to reconcile Michelangelo's art with his difficult personality, bringing to life the story of a man who rose from humble beginnings to favoured artist of the rich and powerful

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Documentary charting jazz musician George Melly's visit to the Hayward Gallery in 1978, where he examines the works on show in a major exhibition on Dada and surrealism. He also talks to some of the last English followers of the movement, including Roland Penrose, before meeting up with rock band the Stranglers

programme.title: Wainwright: The Man Who Loved the Lakes
programme.desc: Part-dramatised profile of writer and artist Alfred Wainwright, the enthusiastic fell-walker from Blackburn who became renowned for his pictorial guides to the English Lake District. More than two million copies have been sold since he began writing them in 1955, and they have become the standard reference work for the area

programme.title: Britain in Focus: A Photographic History
programme.desc: Eamonn McCabe explores the development of the art of photography in the UK, beginning by looking at how science and technology allowed pioneering photographers like Roger Fenton and Julia Margaret Cameron to create a new art form in the 1800s

programme.desc: Coverage of the opening session on day seven, featuring the men's and women's marathons, as the runners start and finish in Victoria Square in the heart of the city, passing through key landmarks. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.sub-title: Countryside and Creation at the Royal Norfolk Show
programme.desc: The Rev Kate Bottley visits the Royal Norfolk Show - one of the largest agricultural events in the country, and one that has been celebrating food and farming in the county for nearly 180 years. There, she meets Christians living out their faith in farming communities across the county. She meets the Bishop of Lynn, the Rt Rev Jane Steen, who explains why having a Christian presence at the show is important and the Rev Dr Tim Weatherstone who is taking on the role of rural chaplain in the county. Anna Mudeka, leader of the African Choir of Norfolk who are performing in the show's Carnival of Cultures, explains the importance of togetherness and talks about the choir's involvement at the archbishop of Canterbury's installation service

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Sarah Moore visits Beaconsfield recycling centre in Buckinghamshire, searching for three items with the potential to be revived. She saves a pine chest of drawers for carpenter Martin Hough and a trio of utility chairs for upcycler Sarah Peterson. Sarah takes on a set of trestle table bases for her own project

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: The Mating Game
programme.desc: Animals for whom the odds of successfully mating are unusually high, including fan-tailed anglerfish in the deep oceans, who will rarely happen upon a mate, and when they do, their bodies literally fuse into one. In southern Russia, toad-headed agamas need to build burrows for their eggs in a landscape of constantly changing sand dunes, while in North America, periodical cicadas emerge from the ground in immense swarms to overwhelm predators and ensure the next generation of ground-dwellers

programme.desc: Adam Henson is in Cumbria with 27-year-old farmer Georgia Hunter and the flock of goats she keeps in partnership with her dad. She explains why the family turned to keeping goats after a particularly bad lambing season and how they decided to turn their fortunes round by producing their own goats' cheese and soap

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow

Fiona explores the castle and its treasures, including a dog portrait by Edwin Landseer that was cut out of a larger canvas and a giant rabbit, and is challenged to put three carved wooden objects in order of value

programme.title: Live Athletics
programme.desc: Gabby Logan presents coverage of the evening session on the seventh and final day from Alexander Stadium. Recently crowned Commonwealth 800m champion Georgia Hunter-Bell and two-time winner of the race Laura Muir will hope to be contenders for Great Britain in the 1500m, which was won by Ireland's Ciara Mageean two years ago. There is also relay action, with the men's and women's 4x400m and mixed 4x100m taking place. Plus, the finals of the men's pole vault and 3,000m steeplechase, and the women's javelin and long jump. With analysis from Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, and commentary by Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe

The search uncovers fantastic properties, including a vast mystery house with enough bedrooms for the family as well as 17 guests to each enjoy one of their own. Away from the search, Alistair meets influencer Aimee, a seasoned global explorer, who along with her partner has chosen to put down roots in rural Scotland by restoring a cottage

Dominic Chinea and Brenton West tackle the restoration of a paraffin camping stove bought in 1957 that comes with memories of family walking adventures and Will Kirk repairs a table bought in Thailand in the 1960s. Hatter Jayesh Vaghela fixes up a tweed flat cap for visitor Mick

programme.desc: Olivia Rodrigo or Sabrina Carpenter? Wales or Iceland? 1980s sport of 1990s sport? As today's teams battle it out, every answer is a 50-50 shot. Jason Manford hosts

At the end of each round, the team with the most points is eliminated until the final two pairs battle for a cash prize. Presented by Alexander Armstrong and Nish Kumar

programme.desc: Nicola and George prepare for Kojo's birthday drinks in the Vic, but just as things seem to be looking up for the pair, a situation escalates which threatens their harmony. Craig is suspended from public duty policing, Avani attempts to play matchmaker, and Amy worries about recent events

programme.title: Panorama
programme.sub-title: Child Maintenance: Parents Under Pressure - Panorama
programme.desc: The Child Maintenance Service is meant to make sure that parents who live apart from their children make regular payments to support them. But it stands accused of doing too little to enforce payments in some cases, leaving parents missing out on money they are legally entitled to. Meanwhile, parents who make payments say calculations done by the CMS can sometimes be wrong or unaffordable, and that mistakes can affect their mental health. Reporter Krupa Padhy meets parents on both sides to ask whether the system is failing both them and their children

programme.title: Scam Interceptors

programme.title: River Hunters
programme.desc: Rick Edwards and Beau Ouimette head to north Wales to investigate waterways that may contain signs of the medieval Welsh Rebellion. Conwy Castle was constructed by Edward I between 1283-1287 after the Welsh Rebellion of 1282-3. The castle was part of a chain of fortifications known as the 'Iron Ring of Castles' and was both a material and symbolic sign of English power and dominance. Edward I selected its site on a high rock perched above the estuary of the River Conwy so that the castle could be supplied by the river in times of siege. They set up their new home in the abandoned White House, but after Little Rock heads to Graceland, the team attempts to save her from a group of super zombies. Director Ruben Fleischer's comedy horror sequel, starring Woody Harrelson, Jesse Eisenberg and Emma Stone

programme.title: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy (2004)
programme.desc: The chauvinistic host of a top-rated American news programme in 1970s San Diego fights for his status and job security when both are threatened by the arrival of an ambitious female reporter, whose determination to become a newsreader leads to a bitter battle of the sexes. Comedy, starring Will Ferrell, Christina Applegate, Fred Willard and Steve Carell

programme.title: Anchorman 2: The Legend Continues (2013)
programme.desc: Arrogant newsreader Ron Burgundy's career is rescued from a drunken slump by an executive for a new 24-hour news channel. Reassembling his team of sidekicks, he swiftly rises from the network's graveyard to become its biggest star with a run of ludicrously sensationalist broadcasts. Comedy sequel, starring Will Ferrell, Christina Applegate, Paul Rudd and Steve Carell

programme.title: Look Who's Talking Too (1990)
programme.desc: Wisecracking toddler Mikey is joined by mischievous baby sister Julie and sibling rivalry inevitably erupts - while their parents have problems of their own to deal with, in the shape of the kids' good-for-nothing uncle. Comedy sequel, starring John Travolta and Kirstie Alley, with the voices of Bruce Willis and Rosanne Barr

programme.title: Look Who's Talking Now (1993)
programme.desc: A family takes in two pet dogs, a scruffy mongrel with discipline problems and a prim and proper pedigree poodle, whose personality clashes create all sorts of mayhem for the household. Comedy sequel, starring John Travolta and Kirstie Alley, plus the voices of Diane Keaton and Danny DeVito as the canine duo
